Results.ReviewText:
I bought the 780 pro a few years ago and have absolutely loved it. I had one issue with the lid warping a bit so I called Traeger customer service and they sent me an entire new lid to fix the problem free of charge and free shipping. With a company that stands behind its products I happily upgraded to the ironwood XL and can say I am 100% happy to have upgraded. 
The Pro was a great starter grill by if you use it a few days a week like I do then the choice to upgrade with the new features, design, and quality of this grill is a no brainer. Clean up with the new grill is so much easier and even the small new features like the grill light, the pellet level monitor that is visible on your phone, and the duel probes are all great features. I also love the super smoke function and can say that my briskets and pork are better on the new ironwood vs the pro. Again, you can find many pellet grills these days but nothing beat the customer service, quality, and overall awesomeness that Traeger offers. I have convinced serval friends and even my father in law to get one and they are all very happy with the purchase.
Results.Title: I love Traeger so much I upgraded!!!

Results.ReviewText: The XL is massive and able to handle all of your cooking needs.  I upgraded from the Pro 34 which was a tough decision, but this Beast includes WiFi which I first thought was ridiculous.  Now I don't know how I grilled without it.

Results.ReviewText: I have owned several pellet grill brands. I have owned Yoder, Memphis, Recteq, Camp Chef and Pitts and Spitts. The engineering and design of the Traeger Ironwood XL surpasses all of them by a long shot. First of all the grease management system is the best I have seen as is the removeable fire pot for cleaning. I have never in all the bands I have owned had a pellet grill put out the amount of good smoke (thin blue smoke) this does even without the super smoke on. With the super smoke on it is out of this word with good smoke production. The controller is definitely the best in the business and the integrated app has options most don't have. The WIFI was very easy to set up and was working within 3 minutes. The lights that come on when the lid is opened are fantastic. Most brands have them in the interior of the grill and are worthless after 2 cooks. These lights are not to the lid on the exterior of the barrel and do not get covered in smoke. The grill when running is very quiet. I have had other brands where I am laying in bed and can hear the blower motor and auger running and were pretty loud. The pop and lock rail system is very awesome. I have bought the front shelf, Basket, drink holder and 2 roll holder/dispensers, One for paper towel and one for butcher paper. I have found the cooking surface to be very even with temp. I have cooked almost everything I always cook and everything has awesome bark and very good smoke flavor. I cooked a brisket overnight and it used about a half hopper of pellets. The lighted pellet hopper and pellet sensor tells the percentage of pellets left and has a low pellet alarm as well. Cleaning after cooking is a breeze, The porcelain grates are easy to clean with a hot cloth and wiped off. After a 12 hour cook very little ash. The fire grate comes out and you can vacuum out under it. I like the pellet auger drops the pellets down into the burn grate so you will never get back burn.
Results.Title: Best design and engineering of any pellet grill

This is my first Traeger. After decades with standard BBQs I decided to take the plunge and ordered the Ironwood XL. I’ve fallen in love with this beast of a machine. Setup was pretty quick and easy but takes two strong guys to lift the main body (If you need to go up or down stairs or more than 20 yards you may need more help). The only setback was it took a couple tries to get it connected to my WiFi. After that we were off and cooking. 
The grill heats up quick and holds temperature well. The insulation is amazing. Even at high temp I can hold my hand on the lid. I like to grill year round so this is important to me. It was 40 degrees and pouring rain a couple days ago and I smoked a ribeye roast with no trouble.
In the first few weeks we’ve done baby backs, ribeye roast, salmon, pork loin, veggies, potatoes - you name it. And it’s all been great!

As of this time, it is true that Traegers cannot connect to a Samsung Galaxy S22 running Android 13 due to the unique encryption methods used on that particular device. However, there is no other known issue like this and the grill should pair successfully with any smartphone that is not outdated. As for the 2.4 GHz requirement, this frequency is used because it has a longer range than 5.0, with the latter being a substantially faster connection, but not necessary for the limited data that is used by the Traeger app. And although it is always important to keep your firmware up to date, it should not be interpreted as there being some specific safety concern that you need to worry about, but rather that we are always trying to come up with ways for making our products even safer. Results.ReviewText:
Best Traeger yet!!!

Background: My father recommended buying a Traeger in 2006 after he purchased one because he was tired of stoking fires in a firebox every 45 minutes for long cooking times. My father and I won several local BBQ competitions. If he recommended a product for this then it must have something going for it. So, I bought the Big Tex smoker and used it for years until a mouse got into the wiring and chewed through most of the wires under the auger. (Yes, the devil was caught and disposed of for the damage he created) after attempting to rewire the damage, the Temperature setting was never the same, so I purchased the Pro 34, 5 years ago. I used the Pro 34 for long cooks only, because the marketing of grill (A.K.A. reverse searing) was longer to complete than a Charcoal grill for steaks. After years of charcoal grilling, I decided to look into direct flame pellet grill for grilling which lead me to the Ironwood XL (It does not do). I just wanted to purchase one type of fuel instead of two (Charcoal and Pellets). I decided to get a different manufacturer for the direct flame pellet grill. (Please Traeger come up with a grill that has direct flame capabilities!) but also purchased the Ironwood XL for my long cooking times because of the changes from the Pro 34 and Ironwood XL are vastly different.

PROS: Lid Gasket for proper seal, Dual-Wall Insulation, Back Draft exhaust, Pellet Sensor, and D2 Controller. It was incredible how much smoke loss there was on the Pro 34 by simply putting a gasket on the lid. The Dual-Wall Insulation definitely helps with keeping the temperature within a 5 +/- degree difference making the smoke times more consistent. You will need to plan ahead until you get used to a more consistent temperature settings. REMEMBER, do not cook by time, always cook by temperature. The Back Draft exhaust system keeps the "warm" smoke in and the "colder" smoke out. This is how they achieve a more smoke flavor than before. Think about simple physics, Heat raises so anyone that has a smoker with a stack instead of back draft, you're losing a lot of good smoke flavor profile because the "good" smoke is simply rising up through and into the stack instead of circulating through the food. Hence the smokestack creosote. I'm not sure about the super smoke setting because you don't need to utilize this setting for long smokes. Like I said before, I use my Traeger for smoking not grilling. I never thought an app was necessary for a grill until I realized that I didn't need to go outside to check the level of pellets. Just use the app for monitoring, BTW I needed to leave for an appointment, and you can still use the app while not connected to the same Wi-Fi network. The pellets got low, so I had my wife add more pellets while I was out. 

CONS: EZ-Clean, Pellet Removal Location, Traeger Website Accessory Items, and Shutdown Procedure. Having the Drip Pan Collect Ash and Grease is great however, not having an Aluminum drip tray option makes no sense to not have for this Smoker. Traeger has made the maintenance easer by not needing to vacuum the ash (You still need to remove everything and use a brush to sweep all the ash into the drip pan) but the Trip tray will need to be cleaned after every cook because if you don't clean it, you'll take twice as long the next time to clean it. I have seen how the smoke comes through the drip tray and you can put an aluminum sheet down, just don't cover the slits around the edge of the pan. You also cannot (very easily) clean the funnel to the drip pan. Hence the need for aluminum. You are required to purchase at least one Traeger StayDry Pellet Bin & Lid to remove the pellets from the smoker. Maybe it would not be much of a Con if it was included with the smokers to utilize this function. Adding a $30 bin shouldn't make that much difference in cost for Traeger. This leads me to my last CON, this isn't really about the usability of the smoker but more about Traeger's Website for accessories. Great example, make sure you do not buy the Meater+, this will not connect to the Traeger's D2 Controller, you need to buy Treager X Meater if you want it to all work with one app instead of 2. Cannot find the Cutting board to go on top of the Pellet Lid, nor can I find the CookTop accessory. The D2 Controller on this smoker says you can pair a device like this but cannot seem to find it on the website. I can only assume it will be available at some point later down the road.

EXPERT ADVICE: If you are a previous pellet smoker user, read the manual. There are a lot of reviews stating that the smoker did not complete the seasoning phase at start up. This happened to me until I read the manual and found out one specific detail that really matters most. That is starting the Traeger with the Lid open as instructed on the older devices. DO NOT do this with this generation of devices. The main reason for this is because of the D2 controller. It has an open Lid sensor that feeds more pellets than normal because it needs to keep temperature and it knows that it will lose temperature because of the lid is opened. (GREAT feature by the way) If you attempt to start the smoker with the lid open it bypasses the startup procedure and feeds way more pellets than needed to start the grill. If the grill drops temperature more than 20 degrees, the lid was open to long and to many pellets where fed into the firebox. It time more time to reset the glow rod to reignite the fire. This also seemed to be an issue with looking at foods for longer periods of time. To be clear, I noticed this being an issue when the lid was open for 20 minutes. Use a probe or open the lid for less than 10 minutes. REMEMBER: "It ain't cooking if you're looking." Do not purchase a pre-built Item. The people at the store are just trying to get the job done and not putting it together like the consumer would. They don't cinch down the bolts and really do not care if there are extra parts after completion. Traeger does include the Tools needed as well so build it yourself.

Results.ReviewText:
I've had the Ironwood XL for a couple months now, and I use it 2-3 time a week.  I purchased this solely with the mindset of having a pellet grill that produces more smoke than what I had (first gen Timberline and a Texas Elite).  It has met that requirement well.  In my opinion, smoked food off this grill tastes closer to what you'd expect from a traditional smoker, and it has the most smoky flavor that I've had to date off a pellet grill, even without the use of Super Smoke.  This thing constantly smokes, even at 275 degrees.  That might be what I love most about it.  Gone are the days of cooking at a super low heat for a few hours to maximize smoke.  

I thought everything was packaged well, and the video instructions available were top-notch.  I was never lost on what to put where.  A screwdriver and wrench were supplied.  Use of the wrench was, at time, difficult in a few spots, but otherwise, assembly was a breeze.  

The controller is cool, although, I would be perfectly happy with it not having a touch screen (I worry about longevity), but it all works well.  I really like that my pre-Traeger Meater probes connect to the controller.  That alone has me using those probes much more than I used to, because I don't have to have the Meater block nearby anymore.  I think the controller is very easy to figure out going through the options and whatnot.  Integration to the app is solid.  I think the app has come a long ways over the years.  

Cleanout is pretty slick.  I feel the days of busting out the shop vac are going to be much fewer and far between.  I'll occasionally take everything apart and just brush the ash into the Ash Keg.  The firepot/box never has anything other than pellets in it (no ash clumps).  Even under the firebox, there's very little that makes it in there.  I was worried about not being able to use foil on the drip tray, but it hasn't been an issue.  Just get yourself a plastic putty knife to scrape everything down into the Ash Keg.  It's super quick to do.  

I like all the large side shelf, although, I am hopeful I can one day get the induction burner to put in there.  I have the front shelf as well, so there is lots of space to work.  

One thing to note that I have experienced twice, but now I know to check.  When cooking at higher heat (350), I've shut the grill down, and I would notice smoke coming out of the cap over the grease drain.  Removing the ash keg I found there was some smoldering ash and grease in there (the first time this happened, the grill had been off for hours before I noticed when I went to cover the grill).  I thought I had let it get too full, but it has happened another time on an empty liner.  So I think you just need to be aware of this.  I check it every time after a cook to be safe.  The smoldering grease smoke makes the grill smell terrible.  Fortunately, by the next cook, it was back to smelling great again.  

All in all, this thing does everything I want, and I've been really happy with it!

First ironwood xl lasted less than 1 week before shorting out due to water leaking in from the rear of the lid (through a loose rivet during manufacturing) and running down into ignitor.  2nd and 3rd units both missing hardware (home depots fault admittedly). The first grill also never succeeded in making it through the initial seasoning burn, which it attempted 3 times.  Ended up just doing this manually by letting it burn for an hour at the highest temp setting. 

 Finally (hopefully) have a functional and complete unit, and nothing but trouble with the required combo wifi/bt/location connection.  The BT signal is too week to stay connected to phone or tablet inside the house even through only 1 wall. For the price point of this grill it should seriously be a lot less hassle,  and have much better quality control.  Unless things improve it will be the last traeger product I ever purchase,  IF we even decide to keep it.  I will highly recommend against this unit and brand to everyone I know. 

Last note, I was going to leave a picture very clearly showing the loose rivet leading to the short on the first unit but the option to leave apic is locked out for me on this review.

Results.ReviewText: Bought the new Ironwood XL as a replacement for a Traeger that was in perfect working order. I just knew when I saw it I had to have it. And it did not disappoint. Absolutely love the new grill. Every cook has been fantastic. I’m super impressed how it holds the smoke in, compared to my old grill. It’s hard to explain but it just cooks a little different. Super impressed. My first cook was fantastic and couldn’t wait till the next one.
Results.Title: Lovin my new Ironwood

Results.Title: Great Product

Results.ReviewText:
Before I received my Ironwood XL, that I purchased of the Traeger website, I had never used a smoker...  I have an amazing Napoleon five burner grill, and have had several nice Webers, so I am very familiar with grilling.

In the few weeks since I received and began using my Traeger Ironwood XL, I have successfully smoked Chickens, ribs, dino ribs, and of course brisket.

I use a combination of Traeger rubs and pellets, and Meat Church's products.

Each of my meat cooks have gone perfectly.  I am the envy of my friends and neighbors, and am gearing up for a few large parties at my estate, where I will handle the meat entrees.

This grill has so many features that with a little practice, you can produce expert results.  I love it.

As much as I love my grill, I will likely upgrade to the Timberline XL sometime...  I have to always have the best of everything.  However, other than the aesthetics, they are very similar.

Thanks Traeger!
Results.Title: The Traeger XL is an amazing product!

Results.ReviewText:
I bought this Ironwood XL when it first came out. Yes the XL is a must! I'm blown away. Not sure ill ever use my Weber again. The meats never dries out. Unreal how much better the food tastes! If you can follow their Traeger recipes online, you can make anything, if you have the patience!

I would advise upgrading and buying the Meater Probe. The ones that come with the grill do not regulate the temps properly. 

Also highly recommend the BBQ Drip Ez Trap for prepping all your meats.

The gasket that was installed around the lid sets this grill apart from the rest that Traeger offers. Due to this gasket, their is no smoke that exits out from the lid
Results.Title: First Traeger...never owned a smoker before

ClientResponses.Response: Thanks for posting feedback on the Ironwood XL. Although some model Traegers can take a little longer to warm up than others, there really shouldn’t be a big variation in cook times from one grill to the next. Anytime you believe that you are having performance issues, it is always a good idea to call into our support line. We can be reached at 1-800-TRAEGER up until 10:00 PM MST everyday of the year.

Results.ReviewText:
I really like the Traeger app and WiFire. I’ve done several cooks. Following Traeger recipes on the Ironwood XL no longer seems wise to me. Temps and times haven’t worked out yet. I use longer times and higher goal temperatures than the recipe calls for. Changing out wood pellets is a pain. Shoot is too far in for a 5 gallon bucket to reach and it takes several times of manually pushing pellets to discharge shoot. Everyone has liked the smoked food flavor.
located in Minnesota and would cautiously recommend Traeger…or not.
Results.Title: Some positive and some negative

Results.ReviewText: Been a Traeger owner for 12 years. This new Ironwood XL is simply amazing. Build quality and new tech are top notch.

Results.ReviewText: I have had smokers before, namely the Yoder YS640 Competition.  I like the Traeger so much better.  I like the full control,m the built in menus, the looks, and the flexibility.  I may never need another cooker, the way I take care of things.  I wish it had aluminum trays for the base.  I would sacrifice cooking longer to keep my grill pristine.  Love the Ironwood XL  Already done ribs, large chickens, and this weekend a couple of large briskets.
